source.title: Serotonin and brain function: a tale of two receptors

confidence_rationale: Provides a well-developed, pharmacologically-anchored case that the two most-studied serotonin receptors are FUNCTIONALLY DISSOCIABLE -- 5-HT1A postsynaptic signalling mediates passive coping / stress moderation, 5-HT2A mediates active coping / plasticity, and they are differentially engaged by SSRIs vs 5-HT2A-agonist psychedelics. This directly grounds Q-075's prediction that the precision/terrain axis maps onto dissociable serotonin subtypes. Discounted because it is a THEORETICAL bipartite synthesis, not a receptor-selective double-dissociation RCT, and Q-075's finer cortical-narrative-vs-hippocampal-terrain assignment is more specific than the paper's coping-style framing.
failure_signatures: The dissociation is argued as a bipartite theoretical model, not demonstrated by a factorial receptor-selective intervention showing a crossover (5-HT2A drug moves axis A but not B, 5-HT1A drug moves B but not A) -- so it supports dissociability without delivering the double-dissociation design Q-075 specifies.

Coping style (passive vs active) is not the same construct as a latent vulnerability AXIS (precision/terrain); if REE's axis does not line up with the coping dimension, the receptor grounding transfers to the wrong variable.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Serotonin enhances two distinct adaptive responses to adversity via its two most prevalent brain receptors: postsynaptic 5-HT1A signalling mediates passive coping (stress moderation, the default response), while 5-HT2A signalling mediates active coping (enhanced plasticity / capacity for change); SSRIs preferentially enhance the 5-HT1A pathway and 5-HT2A-agonist psychedelics the 5-HT2A pathway.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-075 asks whether ARC-086's latent vulnerability axes are grounded in dissociable neuromodulator-receptor systems, predicting the precision/terrain axis maps to serotonin subtypes (5-HT2A-cortical narrative vs 5-HT1A-hippocampal terrain). This paper supplies the receptor-level dissociability that prediction needs: two serotonin receptors with distinct, separately-druggable functional roles, rather than a single serotonergic tone.
mapping.mapping_caveat: OUT-OF-DOMAIN by design: Q-075's test domain is clinical pharmacology, and V3 has no 5-HT receptor subtypes (receptor_subtype_intervention_layer.md Section 4). This entry raises literature grounding only; it promotes/demotes nothing and licenses no V3 experiment. The paper argues dissociable COPING FUNCTIONS, not the specific cortical-narrative/hippocampal-terrain axis assignment Q-075 proposes, and it is a theoretical synthesis rather than a double-dissociation trial.
mapping.source_context: Narrative/theoretical review in clinical psychopharmacology, integrating human and animal pharmacology of SSRIs and serotonergic psychedelics.

confidence_components.notes: Influential, widely-cited synthesis but a theoretical model rather than an interventional double-dissociation (source_quality 0.70). Out-of-domain transfer to REE latent axes and the coping-vs-axis construct gap hold mapping_fidelity/transfer_risk mid-range.
